title: 2019 HMMT February Guts Problem M_{2}
statement: Let \(S=\left\lfloor M_{5}\right\rfloor\). Two integers \(m\) and \(n\) are chosen between 1 and \(S\) inclusive uniformly and independently at random. What is the probability that \(m^{n}=n^{m}\) ?

solutions.text:
\(\frac{7}{72}\)
\(S=12\). The solutions are \((x, x)\) for all \(x\), and \((2,4),(4,2)\). Thus, there are \(S+2=14\) solutions out of \(S^{2}=196\) possibilities, so the answer is \(14 / 144=7 / 72\).
